meta.title: Laceration repair (12001-13153, G0168) — facts declaration + coding data for the bespoke core
meta.derivedFrom: laceration-cleanroom-spec.md (rule numbers cited per entry as specRef)
meta.consumer: laceration-core.ts (bespoke family core). The class cascade, class-dependent site grouping, cross-wound summing, and complex add-on arithmetic exceed the weak table vocabulary, so this file is NOT interpreted by evaluator.ts — but it declares the family's facts in the same style as the reference decision tables, and every code number, band edge, group membership, unit cap, checklist, and payer note lives here as data, not in code.

semantics.siteGroups: Per repair class, the CPT site groupings (spec A3). Group membership is class-dependent: the same base site can change groups when the class changes (hand: S-A simple, I-2 intermediate, C-3 complex).
semantics.bandSeries: Simple/intermediate code ladders (spec A4). 'steps' are ordered; each step's maxCm is the inclusive upper bound of its band (null = unbounded). The core picks the first step whose maxCm >= summed group length.
semantics.complexSeries: Complex base/second/add-on structure per group (spec A4/A6). floorCm is the 1.1 cm complex minimum; add-on units = ceil((L - 7.5) / 5), 'each additional 5 cm or less'.
semantics.unitCaps: Per-code MUE maximum billable units per date of service (spec B4). defaultMaxUnitsPerDay covers every family code not listed in caps (all base repair codes are MUE 1, MAI 2).
semantics.docChecklist: Required documentation for the listed codes; items are human-verified, not computed. codes: ["*"] applies to every emitted code.

vocabulary.sidedSiteKeys: Wound-map keys. Paired sites appear only as '<site>-left' / '<site>-right' (the form offers no side-less option for paired sites); midline sites are bare keys. Legacy convention for imported/pre-sided data ONLY (not offered by the form): '<pairedSite>-unsided' is accepted with full group membership plus a laterality item added to requiredDocumentation. 'other' (or any unrecognized key) yields review-not-authoritative output: no codes, review flag + reason.

facts.name: wounds

lengthCm.description: Measured repair length in cm at time of repair; code-determining — absent (and not strips-only) -> the core refuses. Spec B1.2/A4.

depth.description: Documented closure depth/material class; drives the class cascade. Code-determining: absent -> refuse. Spec A1/A2.

complexElements.description: CPT complex-repair qualifying elements documented for THIS wound; only upgrades a layered closure. Spec A2.

contaminated.description: Heavy contamination AND extensive cleaning BOTH documented — the single-layer -> intermediate route. Spec A2.

facts.description: Every wound repaired this encounter, keyed by sided site; lengths sum within one class + site group, never across. Spec A5.1/A5.2.

facts.name: closure_material
facts.description: Closure material/method as documented; never code-determining but required documentation for every repair code. Spec B1.3.

facts.name: suture_count
facts.description: Documented suture/staple count; completeness item only (never blocks).

facts.name: irrigation
facts.description: Wound irrigation documented; completeness item only. (tetanus_status removed round-2 — lives in the immunization record; the checklist item stays.) Spec A7.

facts.name: payer_type
facts.description: Drives the adhesive-only rule: Medicare + adhesive-sole closure -> G0168; otherwise CPT code + payer note. Spec A1.4/A1.7.

facts.name: adjacent_tissue_transfer
facts.description: Scope gate: flap/Z-plasty/tissue-rearrangement closure is 14xxx ATT territory — repair codes are not reportable for the same injury (true -> no codes, review). Spec A1.8.

siteVocabulary.note: Normalization guidance (spec A3 note): trunk includes chest/back/abdomen/flank/buttock; arm includes shoulder-wrist; leg includes thigh-ankle; hand includes fingers/palm; foot includes toes/heel/sole; mouth = intraoral mucous membranes.

tables.note: Class-dependent membership — the most error-prone rule of the family: eyelid/nose/ear/lip go to C-4, all other face parts to C-3. Spec A3.
Trunk pattern has NO 5.0 split; face pattern (S-B and I-3) adds it. I-3 including 12053 is a KNOWN divergence from the legacy engine; code-number gaps are real. Spec A4.
base 1.1-2.5, second 2.6-7.5, addOn units = ceil((L-7.5)/5) pairing ONLY with the group's second code; below floorCm fall back to intermediate. Spec A4/A6/B3.3.

tables.defaultNote: Every simple/intermediate code and every complex base/second code is MUE 1 per day (MAI 2, Anatomic Consideration) — summing, never multiple units. CMS MUE practitioner table eff. 2026-10-01.

required: Anatomic site of each wound, specific enough to resolve the site group
Measured length in cm of each wound, at time of repair — not estimated
Depth / tissue layers closed — which layers, how many
Per-wound detail when multiple wounds, so lengths can be summed
Defense tier (never code-determining): suture count, tetanus status, irrigation
Single-layer closure; superficial depth with no significant deeper involvement

Layered closure naming the deeper layer(s) closed plus skin closure; OR limited undermining with its extent; OR single-layer closure of a heavily contaminated wound with the extensive cleaning described

Intermediate-level documentation plus at least one qualifying element described concretely (exposed structure, edge debridement, undermining extent, free margin, retention sutures); total complex length at least 1.1 cm
Everything for the base code; total group length over 7.5 cm with units consistent with it; claim carries the group's large base code
Medicare beneficiary; tissue adhesive was the SOLE closure material — no sutures or staples
